name: BQ25173DSGR
title: BQ25173: 800 mA linear charger for 1- to 4-cell supercapacitors
summary: A linear charger for stacks of one to four supercapacitor cells, in a 2 × 2 mm WSON-8. Two resistors set the target voltage through FB (0.8 V reference, ±1 %) and one sets the charge current, 10 mA to 800 mA (±10 %). It charges from 0 V at constant current, then holds the set voltage with no termination, and throttles current to hold the die at 125 °C. IN works from 3.0 V to 18 V and survives 40 V; open-drain STAT and /PG outputs, an active-low enable, input overvoltage, output overcurrent and ISET short protection are built in.

pins.name: IN
pins.function: Supply input from the external DC source. Decouple to GND with 1 µF or more, close to the IC.

pins.name: ISET
pins.function: A resistor from this pin to GND sets the fast-charge current, ICHG = KISET / RISET; 30 kΩ gives 10 mA and 375 Ω gives 800 mA.

pins.name: /CE
pins.function: Charge enable, active low. Low allows charging; high holds the IC in shutdown with charging off. An internal pulldown (RPD_CE) enables the part when the pin floats.

pins.name: STAT
pins.function: Open-drain charge status. Pull up with 10 kΩ. Low once VOUT reaches 98 % of VREG; high while charging is under way; blinks at 1 Hz on a fault.

pins.name: /PG
pins.function: Open-drain power-good. Pull up with 10 kΩ. Goes low once the input is good: VIN exceeds both VIN_LOWV and VOUT + VSLEEPZ, and stays under VIN_OV.

pins.name: FB
pins.function: Feedback for the regulation voltage VREG, from a divider of 1 MΩ or less between OUT and GND. For VREG ≤ 5 V the divider's lower end may return to /PG so the divider draws nothing from OUT once input power is gone.

pins.name: OUT
pins.function: Output to the supercapacitor; a system load may sit in parallel with it. Decouple to GND with 1 µF or more, close to the IC.

pins.name: Thermal Pad
pins.function: Exposed pad under the package for heat removal. Solder it to the board, with vias down to a solid GND plane.

circuits.title: 1s supercapacitor charger, 2.4 V, 800 mA
circuits.description: A single supercapacitor cell is charged to 2.4 V at up to 800 mA from a 5 V to 18 V supply. R1 (375 Ω) on ISET sets 800 mA. R2 and R3 (604 kΩ over 301 kΩ) divide OUT down to FB, giving 0.8 V × 905/301 ≈ 2.4 V; the lower resistor returns to /PG instead of GND, so the divider stops drawing from the cell once input power is removed. STAT and /PG each light an LED from VREF through 10 kΩ. A host drives /CE with an open-drain output. C1 and C2 (1 µF) decouple IN and OUT.

parts.note: one cell with a resistor across it

notes: Design targets: 5 V to 18 V supply, ICHG = 800 mA, VREG = 2.4 V, /CE driven open-drain, /PG used as the divider's ground return.

circuits.title: 4s supercapacitor charger, 8.8 V, 500 mA
circuits.description: A stack of four series supercapacitor cells, each with a balancing resistor across it, is charged to 8.8 V (2.2 V a cell) at 500 mA from a 9 V to 18 V supply. R1 (600 Ω) on ISET sets 500 mA. R2 and R3 (806 kΩ over 80.6 kΩ) set 0.8 V × 886.6/80.6 ≈ 8.8 V; with VREG above 5 V the divider returns to GND, not /PG. STAT and /PG each light an LED from VREF through 10 kΩ. A host pulls /CE high to stop charging. C1 and C2 (1 µF) decouple IN and OUT.

parts.note: four cells in series, a balancing resistor across each

notes: Design targets: 9 V to 18 V supply, ICHG = 500 mA, VREG = 8.8 V, /CE pulled high to disable charging.

operation.text: One pass path runs from IN to OUT, made of two back-to-back FETs, and charges the supercapacitor directly. Any system load connects at OUT beside the supercapacitor and takes its share of the charge current. Current sensing and the power stage are on chip; only the ISET resistor and the FB divider set the charge.

Charging starts from as low as 0 V at the ISET current (constant current) and switches to holding VREG (constant voltage) as OUT arrives there; the current then falls toward zero. Unlike a Li-ion charger there is no termination current: the part keeps regulating at VREG. Dissipation is highest early in fast charge, when OUT is low; if TJ reaches TREG the current is cut back to hold the temperature, so at low ISET settings thermal regulation never engages.

With a valid VIN and /CE low the part brings up its bias, then checks ISET before starting the linear stage. An ISET resistance below RISET_SHORT is a short: the charger stays in fault until VIN or /CE is cycled. An open ISET is accepted and the charger starts with zero charge current. ISET is watched throughout charging, so changing RISET changes ICHG at once.
Below 50 mA an added RC network on ISET is advised for a steadier current. At low currents part of the sense FET is switched off to improve resolution.

/PG pulls low when VIN is above VIN_LOWV, above VOUT + VSLEEPZ (not asleep) and below VIN_OV. Because /PG floats when input power is gone, returning the FB divider's lower resistor to /PG stops the divider draining the supercapacitor; this suits VREG ≤ 5 V (1 or 2 cells) only, since /PG is rated to 5.5 V.
STAT is open drain and can drive an LED. It stays high while VFB is under 98 % of VFB_REF, goes low above that, and blinks at 1 Hz on a fault: input overvoltage, output overcurrent or a shorted ISET.
IN above VIN_OV puts the part in standby; charging restarts by itself once IN returns to the normal range.

OUT current normally sits at the ISET value, but a shorted ISET could let it climb. If it exceeds IOUT_OCP for longer than tOUT_OCP_DGL the part switches off and latches; cycling VIN or /CE restarts it.

Above TREG the charge current is reduced to hold the junction at TREG, so the delivered current is then below the ISET setting. Above TSHUT the linear stage turns off, and it restarts once the die cools below the TSHUT falling threshold. Normal operation at nominal input and ambient is best kept out of thermal regulation, which is meant for hot or high-input cases, though the part works correctly with it engaged all the time.

Shutdown (UVLO): VIN below VIN_LOWV; internal circuits off and pins high impedance. Sleep: VIN_LOWV < VIN < VOUT + VSLEEPZ; the part waits for VIN to clear VOUT + VSLEEPZ. Active: /CE low, with VIN clear of VIN_LOWV as well as of VOUT + VSLEEPZ; the part charges and draws IQ_IN. Standby: valid input with a recoverable fault; partly biased while it watches for the fault to clear. Fault: VIN OVP recovers by itself; OUT OCP and a shorted ISET need a /CE or input toggle.

The supply runs from 3.0 V to 18 V (IN survives 40 V) and should deliver at least the highest programmed charge current. A supply more than a few inches from IN and GND calls for a larger input capacitor.

Put the IN and OUT capacitors as close to the part as possible with short traces to IN, OUT and GND. Keep small-signal ground returns apart from the supercapacitor's high-current paths and join them at a single point. Size the IN and OUT traces for the full charge current so they drop little voltage.
